the squared ratio of two-phase mixture volume to mixture speed of sound is the weighted mean of the saturated liquid and saturated vapor values and that a simplified method of determining two-phase Mach numbers for various flows can be developed using these values.

the two-phase sound speed ratio 0(g,7) can be represented as the weighted mean of the saturated liquid and vapor sound speeds, 0(1,7), 0(0,T) and that this property, 0(g,T), is a good approximation of the two-phase sound speeds ratio for the nitrogen two-phase flows investigated.
the two-phase Mach number for equilibrium flow of nitrogen is the same as the mean two-phase properties and that a simple method is developed to compute this two-phase Mach number.

two-phase flow through a duct with equilibrium vaporization.
the development of a method of predicting two-phase Mach numbers and the associated Mach number jumps at a phase boundary for equilibrium duct flow of nitrogen.
a new method of describing the two-phase Mach number for equilibrium flow of nitrogen and with a simplified method of determining this number for various two-phase duct flows.

the present analysis is a significant contribution to two-phase flow research and that the results are of practical importance.
the two-phase Mach number concept, as developed for equilibrium two-phase flow, is a useful and convenient method for the calculation of two-phase flow duct problems.
the two-phase Mach number description is a very useful and powerful tool for two-phase duct flows.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the isentropic two-phase flow Mach number is a function of only two variables: the liquid mass fraction at the phase boundary and the ratio of the liquid and vapor sound speeds at the phase boundary.
we have developed a simple and accurate method for calculating two-phase flow Mach numbers and Mach number jumps.
the isothermal saturated vapor and liquid sound speeds can be used to calculate the two-phase sound speed for equilibrium flow and the Mach number for equilibrium duct flow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the isothermal two-phase properties are sufficient to calculate the Mach number for equilibrium flow.
